lines.text: More trees, or more stars? Guess first.
lines.phonemes: mˈɔːɹ tɹˈiːz, ɔːɹ mˈɔːɹ stˈɑːɹz? ɡˈɛs fˈɜːst.

lines.text: Our galaxy has hundreds of billions of stars. Nobody counted them. Most of its weight is dark matter, so stars are a small part.
lines.phonemes: ˌaʊɚ ɡˈælɐksi hɐz hˈʌndɹɪdz ʌv bˈɪliənz ʌv stˈɑːɹz. nˈoʊbɑːdi kˈaʊntᵻd ðˌɛm. mˈoʊst əv ɪts wˈeɪt ɪz dˈɑːɹk mˈæɾɚ, sˌoʊ stˈɑːɹz ɑːɹ ɐ smˈɔːl pˈɑːɹt.

lines.text: Now the trees. In twenty fifteen, a team put Earth's at about three trillion. That's hundreds of trees for every person alive.
lines.phonemes: nˈaʊ ðə tɹˈiːz. ɪn twˈɛnti fˈɪftiːn, ɐ tˈiːm pˌʊt ˈɜːθz æɾ ɐbˌaʊt θɹˈiː tɹˈɪliən. ðæts hˈʌndɹɪdz ʌv tɹˈiːz fɔːɹ ˈɛvɹi pˈɜːsən ɐlˈaɪv.

lines.text: Researchers counted trees in ground plots, then scaled up with satellite maps. Both are estimates, not exact counts, so each really means about. The honest answer is a range.
lines.phonemes: ɹᵻsˈɜːtʃɚz kˈaʊntᵻd tɹˈiːz ɪn ɡɹˈaʊnd plˈɑːts, ðˈɛn skˈeɪld ˌʌp wɪð sˈæɾəlˌaɪt mˈæps. bˈoʊθ ɑːɹ ˈɛstᵻməts, nˌɑːt ɛɡzˈækt kˈaʊnts, sˌoʊ ˈiːtʃ ɹˈiəli mˈiːnz ɐbˈaʊt. ðɪ ˈɑːnɪst ˈænsɚɹ ɪz ɐ ɹˈeɪndʒ.

lines.text: Now turn every star into a tree. The stars run out, and Earth's forests keep going. Trees win, by roughly eight to thirty times. Quick thing: if that made the sky feel bigger, tap like and follow.
lines.phonemes: nˈaʊ tˈɜːn ˈɛvɹi stˈɑːɹ ˌɪntʊ ɐ tɹˈiː. ðə stˈɑːɹz ɹˈʌn ˈaʊt, ænd ˈɜːθz fˈɔːɹɪsts kˈiːp ɡˈoʊɪŋ. tɹˈiːz wˈɪn, baɪ ɹˈʌfli ˈeɪt tə θˈɜːɾi tˈaɪmz. kwˈɪk θˈɪŋ: ɪf ðæt mˌeɪd ðə skˈaɪ fˈiːl bˈɪɡɚ, tˈæp lˈaɪk ænd fˈɑːloʊ.

lines.text: There are more trees on Earth than stars in our galaxy. Big numbers hide in ordinary places.
lines.phonemes: ðɛɹˌɑːɹ mˈɔːɹ tɹˈiːz ˌɔn ˈɜːθ ðɐn stˈɑːɹz ɪn ˌaʊɚ ɡˈælɐksi. bˈɪɡ nˈʌmbɚz hˈaɪd ɪn ˈɔːɹdɪnˌɛɹi plˈeɪsᵻz.

lines.text: Light time across our galaxy: longer than all of written history. Across a city block: about a millionth of a second.
lines.phonemes: lˈaɪt tˈaɪm əkɹˌɑːs ˌaʊɚ ɡˈælɐksi: lˈɔŋɡɚ ðɐn ˈɔːl ʌv ɹˈɪʔn hˈɪstɚɹi. əkɹˌɑːs ɐ sˈɪɾi blˈɑːk: ɐbˌaʊt ɐ mˈɪliənθ əvə sˈɛkənd.

lines.text: Next: with that many stars, why is the night sky dark?
lines.phonemes: nˈɛkst: wɪð ðæt mˈɛni stˈɑːɹz, wˌaɪ ɪz ðə nˈaɪt skˈaɪ dˈɑːɹk?
